data.title: Waymo is coming to Canada, with Toronto robotaxi service planned for 2028
data.description:
Waymo is officially coming to Canada, announcing plans to launch its fully autonomous ride-hailing service in Toronto in 2028. The Alphabet-owned company will begin testing vehicles on Toronto streets in the coming days, marking its first expansion into the Canadian market.

As with its expansion into any new city, the initial phase will see Waymo vehicles driven manually to map local roads before progressing to autonomous testing with trained safety specialists behind the wheel. The company is also establishing local facilities and expects to create hundreds of jobs as it prepares for commercial operations.

Waymo has been steadily expanding its robotaxi network across the United States, while Tesla has been growing its own Robotaxi service since launching in Austin in June 2025.

Waymo partners with Canadian fleet operator

To support its Canadian launch, Waymo is expanding its partnership with Toronto-based Element Fleet Management, which already supports its operations in San Diego.

Element will oversee fleet maintenance, charging infrastructure, vehicle cleaning, and other daily operations needed to keep the robotaxis running.

Waymo says its autonomous vehicles have travelled more than 400 million kilometres without a human driver, with 95% fewer crashes involving serious injuries or worse compared to human drivers in its operating markets.

data.title: Global EV Sales Fall in September as Europe Hits Record Highs
data.description:
Global electric vehicle sales declined in September 2026, bringing an end to six consecutive months of growth as weaker demand in China and North America outweighed record-breaking sales in Europe.

According to data from Benchmark Mineral Intelligence reported by Reuters, global EV sales reached 2.15 million units in September, down 2% compared to the same month last year. Despite the decline, worldwide sales are still up 3% through the first nine months of 2026, reaching 15.5 million vehicles.

The slowdown comes as the EV market continues to adjust to changing government incentives. U.S. EV sales surged in the third quarter of 2025 as buyers rushed to take advantage of federal tax credits before they expired, making September 2025 a record month and creating a difficult comparison for automakers this year.

Canada has seen a different trend following the return of federal EV rebates in February. Registrations climbed 26.7% year over year in the second quarter, with 58,811 zero-emission vehicles registered, representing 10.7% of new vehicles.

Europe was September’s standout performer. Per Electrek‘s breakdown of the Benchmark data, sales climbed 39% to nearly 600,000 vehicles, a new monthly record. Germany recorded 117,000 sales, up 61%, while France jumped 78% to nearly 80,000. The UK, Spain, Portugal, and Finland also set monthly records.

China remained the largest market at 1.11 million vehicles, but sales fell 18% year over year. North America experienced an even sharper decline of 44%, with approximately 130,000 vehicles sold.

However, with China slowing and Europe accelerating, the global EV market is heading into the final quarter of 2026 with increasingly different regional trends.

data.title: U.S. Built Vehicle Sales Slide in Canada as Tesla and Others Shift Production
data.description:
American-made vehicles are losing ground in Canada, with new data showing their share of the Canadian auto market dropped sharply during the first half of 2026 as tariffs forced automakers to rethink where they source their vehicles.

According to J.D. Power Canada data reported by The Globe and Mail, U.S.-built vehicles accounted for just 28.4% of new vehicle sales between January and June, down from 35.4% during the same period last year. That’s a 7-percentage-point decline, or nearly 20% of their previous market share.

Tesla has been one of the clearest examples of this shift. As Drive Tesla previously reported, the automaker moved Canadian Model Y supply from the United States to Giga Berlin to avoid Ottawa’s 25% counter-tariffs.

The change allowed Tesla to slash Model Y prices by $20,000. More recently, Tesla also began importing Shanghai-built Model 3 sedans under Canada’s new Chinese EV quota, which allows 49,000 vehicles annually at a 6.1% tariff.

The move was so popular Tesla forced the government’s hand to limit the number of vehicles Tesla could import over a fear they would leave none for other automakers.

Mexico and Japan Gain Market Share

The latest figures show Mexico benefiting significantly from these changes, with its share climbing from 18.3% to 22.2%, according to J.D. Power figures. Japan also gained ground, increasing from 13.7% to 16.6%, while South Korea rose from 14.6% to 15.6%.

Meanwhile, Canadian-built vehicles accounted for 11.5% of sales, down 9% year-over-year.

“Our data shows the largest change for vehicles coming out of the U.S.,” said Robert Karwel, director of OEM Solutions with J.D. Power in Canada.

Tesla isn’t alone. Mazda stopped Canadian sales of its Alabama-built CX-50, while Volvo halted imports of its South Carolina-built EX90.

Despite the decline, American-made vehicles still hold the largest individual share of Canada’s market. However, with tariffs remaining in place and manufacturers increasingly sourcing vehicles elsewhere, the shift away from U.S. production could continue into 2027.

data.title: Tesla Wants to Jump the Roadster Across Snake River Canyon in Evel Knievel-Inspired Stunt
data.description:
Tesla’s newly revealed Roadster could be headed for one of the most ambitious automotive stunts ever attempted. During Thursday’s unveiling at SpaceX’s McGregor, Texas test facility, Elon Musk suggested the company could attempt to fly the electric sports car across Idaho’s Snake River Canyon.

The idea would recreate Evel Knievel’s infamous 1974 attempt to cross the canyon, but this time using a Tesla Roadster equipped with a compressed-gas thruster system capable of lifting the vehicle off the ground.

Knievel’s original attempt involved a steam-powered rocket called the Skycycle X-2. The stunt ended in failure when its parachute deployed prematurely, sending Knievel down into the canyon. He survived, but the attempted jump became one of the most memorable moments of his career.

Tesla has spent years promising that its next-generation Roadster would offer capabilities beyond those of a conventional sports car. Those promises finally became reality during the October 15 unveiling, when the company demonstrated the Roadster flying twice in front of an audience.

Near the end of the livestream, Musk floated the possibility of taking things even further.

“So we’re going to have actually a follow-on demo… I don’t know if this is possible or not, but some people may know about Evel Knievel’s attempt to jump the Snake River Canyon.”

The response on stage was immediate: “Oh yeah, let’s give it another shot.”

The discussion then turned to speed. Tesla says the Roadster’s Rocket configuration can exceed 230 mph (370 km/h), but Musk suggested the canyon attempt could require something closer to Mach 0.5, roughly half the speed of sound.

“Where we’re going you don’t need tires,” Musk joked.

No date or specific plans were announced for the stunt. Tesla also hasn’t confirmed whether the idea will become an official demonstration.

For now, the company’s focus remains on bringing the Roadster into production in 2028.

data.title: Tesla Roadster’s Fan Suction System Generates Enough Downforce to Hold It Upside Down
data.description:
Tesla has revealed more details about the new Roadster‘s aerodynamic system, including powerful fans capable of generating enough suction to hold the electric sports car upside down while stationary.

Unveiled on on Thursday night, the next-generation Roadster combines a ground-effect suction system, active aerodynamics, and SpaceX-inspired cold-gas thrusters. Tesla says the technology will allow the car to achieve extraordinary levels of traction and cornering performance, even at low speeds.

The Roadster has been one of Tesla’s most anticipated vehicles since its original unveiling in 2017. Elon Musk has repeatedly promised performance beyond conventional sports cars, including a SpaceX package that would use thrusters to improve acceleration and handling. Now, nearly nine years later, Tesla has provided its clearest explanation yet of how those technologies work together.

Downforce Without Speed

Unlike traditional aerodynamic systems that rely on airflow generated by vehicle speed, the Roadster uses powered fans to pull air from underneath the car, as we first saw in a patent earlier this year. Combined with seals around the underbody, the system creates suction that pushes the vehicle against the road.

“We have a fan suction system on the bottom of the car that can pull up to two g’s in order to make the car go upside down. And then we borrowed some technology from SpaceX to do the rest,” Musk explained during the unveiling.

Tesla says the system can generate enough downforce to support cornering forces exceeding 2 g, compared with the roughly 1.26 g typically available from the tires alone.

During the demonstration on Thursday night, the system generated over 4,700 kg of downforce, enough to keep it stuck to the “road” while upside down.

The suction system operates in two modes, increasing traction at low speeds before opening front and rear airflow passages to improve performance at higher speeds.

The Roadster also features an adjustable rear wing, with actuators derived from Tesla’s Optimus robot program. Its angle changes automatically to balance downforce and aerodynamic drag.

Roadster transforms in Track Mode These aero features aren’t just for looks: they provide the best passive downforce package of any road car (approaching F1 levels!) with wing actuation driven by the @Tesla_Optimus actuator system https://t.co/AqrC4qUga9

— Tesla (@Tesla) October 16, 2026

Meanwhile, cold-gas thrusters provide rapid stabilization adjustments, including when the vehicle is airborne.

data.title: Tesla’s Roadster Can Actually Fly – Here’s How
data.description:
Tesla has officially unveiled its next-generation Roadster, confirming the electric sports car will use technology borrowed from SpaceX to deliver acceleration unlike anything currently on the road. In its most extreme configuration, the Roadster will even be capable of flight.

During an unveiling event on Thursday, Tesla revealed three versions of the Roadster, including a Rocket variant capable of accelerating from 0 to 60 mph in less than 0.59 seconds. CEO Elon Musk also confirmed that production is scheduled to begin in 2028.

The Roadster was first unveiled in 2017, with Musk promising a 0-60 mph time of 1.9 seconds and a range of 620 miles. Since then, the project has experienced numerous delays, while Musk continued teasing a SpaceX package that would take its performance well beyond conventional sports cars. Now we know exactly what that package involves.

HOLY SHIT! That was not real….but it was….🤯 Roadster really can fly! https://t.co/Su4VzF5XXR

— Drive Tesla 🇨🇦 (@DriveTeslaca) October 16, 2026

Tesla says the Roadster uses carbon-fibre overwrapped pressure vessels (COPVs) to store compressed air, which is released through cold-gas thrusters. The system includes two tanks with a combined 600-litre capacity, approximately 250 kilograms of air, and 10 nozzles.

Unlike traditional rockets, the system doesn’t require specialized propellant. The car can recharge its own air tanks, allowing the Roadster to perform repeated manoeuvres.

Tesla says the thrusters can generate four to five times the force available through conventional tire grip. The Rocket variant uses perimeter-mounted thrusters for acceleration, lift, and aerial manoeuvres, while electric actuators make rapid adjustments to stabilize the vehicle in flight.

The lineup will include a two-seat Performance version, a two-seat Thrust variant with rear-mounted thrusters that Tesla says can reach 60 mph in under 0.9 seconds, and a single-seat Rocket model. Tesla is targeting more than 300 miles of range, with a top speed exceeding 230 mph for the Rocket.

Despite the extraordinary claims, Musk acknowledged the potential risks during the livestream, saying, “I should say that this is not necessarily a safety-optimized car.”

With production still two years away, questions remain about pricing, regulatory approval, and how much of the Roadster’s promised performance will translate into customer vehicles.

data.title: Tesla Roadster finally revealed with thrusters, sub-one-second acceleration and ability to fly…actually
data.description:
Tesla has finally unveiled its long-awaited next-generation Roadster, and it is unlike anything the company has built before. Revealed at SpaceX’s McGregor facility in Texas, the electric sports car features rocket-inspired thrusters, extreme acceleration, and, in its most advanced configuration, the ability to actually fly.

The unveiling included something we never thought we’d say about a car – two flight demonstrations.

Following the event, Tesla confirmed three Roadster configurations will be available, with acceleration times as quick as 0-60 mph in under 0.59 seconds and production scheduled to begin in 2028 – for real this time according to CEO Elon Musk.

Three versions, including one that flies

The next-generation Roadster will come in three variants – if you can afford it.

The “base” entry-level Performance version seats two and uses active aerodynamics and a suction system to generate additional downforce. Tesla claims it can accelerate from 0-60 mph in under 1.6 seconds.

The Thrust configuration adds rear-mounted cold-gas thrusters, reducing that time to under 0.9 seconds.

At the top of the lineup is the single-seat Rocket, featuring additional thrusters capable of lifting the vehicle off the ground and controlling its movement in flight. Tesla claims a 0-60 mph time under 0.59 seconds and a top speed exceeding 230 mph (370 km/h), while all versions are rated for more than 300 miles (480 km) of range.

HOLY SHIT! That was not real….but it was….🤯 Roadster really can fly! https://t.co/Su4VzF5XXR

— Drive Tesla 🇨🇦 (@DriveTeslaca) October 16, 2026

After the car lifted off during the demonstration, Musk declared, “Flying cars are real.” He also teased an even bigger stunt to come, an attempt at Evel Knievel’s famous Snake River Canyon jump.

The technology relies on compressed air stored in carbon fibre pressure vessels, rather than conventional rocket fuel.

If that wasn’t enough, the @Tesla Roadster just did a ‘kickflip’ over the entire Tesla lineup, including the Semi! https://t.co/xUUsDVBNao

— Drive Tesla 🇨🇦 (@DriveTeslaca) October 16, 2026

How much will the Roadster cost?

Canadian reservation payments are now listed at $70,000 for Performance and $350,000 for Thrust. Interested buyers in the U.S. will have to put down US$50,000 and US$250,000 for those configurations respectively. These are reservation amounts, and not the final price, which is still to be announced.

The Rocket is invitation-only with no deposit amount listed and is not approved for public road use.

Nearly a decade in the making

Tesla originally unveiled the second-generation Roadster in 2017, promising a 0-60 mph time of 1.9 seconds and a 620-mile range. However, the project experienced repeated delays as Tesla focused on higher-volume vehicles, including the Model Y and Cybertruck.

The new Roadster takes a dramatically different approach, combining traditional electric performance with technology developed alongside SpaceX.

data.title: Southwest Airlines Aims to Become First Major US Airline With Fleetwide Starlink Wi-Fi in 2027
data.description:
Southwest Airlines has confirmed plans to bring SpaceX’s Starlink internet service to its entire fleet by fall 2027. If it reaches that goal, Southwest will become the first major US airline to complete a fleetwide rollout of the satellite-based technology.

The announcement came Thursday as part of a broader overhaul of Southwest’s Rapid Rewards loyalty program. Once installed, Starlink will provide passengers with high-speed internet from takeoff to landing, with access remaining free for Rapid Rewards members through the airline’s partnership with T-Mobile.

Southwest first announced its Starlink plans earlier this year, targeting more than 300 equipped aircraft by the end of 2026. The latest announcement provides a firm target for completing the rollout across its fleet.

The airline joins a growing list of carriers adopting SpaceX’s satellite internet service. As Drive Tesla previously reported, United Airlines had already equipped more than 300 regional aircraft with Starlink by February 2026, and earlier today announced it has more than doubled that figure.

Southwest’s rollout covers its Boeing 737 fleet. Unlike traditional inflight internet systems, Starlink uses a network of low-Earth orbit satellites to deliver faster connections with lower latency, and passengers can use the service for streaming, video calls, browsing, and other online activities that have historically been difficult with conventional aircraft Wi-Fi.

The connectivity upgrade is one part of Southwest’s wider changes coming in 2027, including new Silver, Gold, and Platinum loyalty tiers, expanded international airline partnerships, and premium airport lounges.

data.title: Tesla Model Y remains California’s best-selling vehicle despite 10% drop in Tesla sales
data.description:
Tesla’s Model Y continues to dominate California’s new vehicle market, holding onto its position as the state’s best-selling vehicle through the first nine months of 2026. However, Tesla’s overall registrations have declined even as the broader California auto market returned to growth in the third quarter.

According to the latest California Auto Outlook report from the California New Car Dealers Association (CNCDA), using data from Experian Automotive, Tesla recorded 121,822 registrations through September, down 10% from 135,293 during the same period last year.

Source: CNCDA / Experian Automotive

California has historically been one of Tesla’s strongest markets, with the Model Y regularly outperforming gasoline-powered competitors. Despite increased competition and changing EV incentives, the electric SUV continues to lead the state’s sales rankings.

Model Y maintains its lead as Tesla sales decline

The Model Y continued its trend of outselling even the most popular gas-powered cars, recording 86,099 registrations through September. Even though sales declined, this was still comfortably ahead of the Toyota Camry at 52,224 and Honda Civic at 42,238.

The Model Y also captured an impressive 57.9% of California’s luxury compact SUV segment.

The Model 3 added another 27,303 registrations, giving Tesla two of the state’s most popular electric vehicles.

January–September 2026. Source: CNCDA / Experian Automotive

However, Tesla’s third-quarter performance tells a different story. Registrations fell 15.4% year-over-year, from 52,005 to 43,994, while its quarterly market share dropped from 11.9% to 9.7%. That slide left Tesla third among California brands through September with a 9.3% share, down from 9.9% last year, behind Toyota and Honda.

The decline came as California’s overall new vehicle market grew 3.9% during the quarter, its first quarterly increase of 2026.

Meanwhile, zero-emission vehicle (ZEV) registrations fell 26.1% year-to-date to 215,467 units, with market share settling at 16.4%. In the third quarter alone, ZEV share eased to 17.3% from 17.9% in the second quarter. Hybrids continued gaining ground, reaching a record 22.8% share through September.

Despite the slowdown, California remains the country’s largest EV market, accounting for 28.9% of nationwide ZEV registrations.

California’s new MyFirstEV rebate program could help support demand in the fourth quarter. Whether that translates into stronger Tesla registrations remains to be seen, but the Model Y’s commanding lead shows it still remains a favourite among California buyers.

data.title: United Airlines Expands Starlink Wi-Fi to Nearly Half of All Flights, Launches New Tracking Tool
data.description:
United Airlines has reached another major milestone in its Starlink rollout, with SpaceX’s satellite internet service now available on nearly half of the airline’s daily flights. The carrier has also launched a new online tool allowing passengers to check whether their upcoming flight will have Starlink connectivity.

According to United, more than 635 aircraft are now equipped with Starlink, serving over 250,000 passengers daily across more than 2,500 flights. The airline is continuing installations at a pace of approximately 20 aircraft per week.

United’s Starlink rollout began in May 2025 with its regional Embraer E175 jets, following FAA certification earlier that year. By February 2026, the airline had surpassed 300 equipped aircraft, covering more than 25% of daily departures. Starlink has since expanded to larger aircraft, including transatlantic routes.

The latest addition is the Starlink Tracker, which allows passengers to enter their flight number and travel date within three days of departure to check connectivity availability. The tool also provides daily installation statistics, aircraft breakdowns, and Starlink coverage percentages across United’s seven major hubs.

The numbers highlight just how quickly the service is expanding. United says more than 37.7 million passengers have travelled aboard Starlink-equipped aircraft across more than 538,000 flights, connecting 14 million devices.

United expects to complete its fleetwide Starlink installations by the end of 2027. Competition is also increasing, with American Airlines recently expanding its own Starlink agreement to cover more than 1,030 aircraft.
